holidays.name: National Coffee Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A day for people who can't decide between dessert and their morning caffeine fix. Scoop up coffee-flavored ice cream and enjoy a chilled jolt of java in every bite.
holidays.origin: Like many American food observances, it grew out of food-industry promotion and social media enthusiasm rather than any official proclamation. It is listed in national food day calendars.
holidays.funFact: Coffee ice cream has been popular in the United States for generations, and in New England it is a classic parlor flavor, often served in local ice cream shops.

holidays.name: Fight Procrastination Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to finally doing that thing you've been putting off. Ironically, many people plan to celebrate it tomorrow.
holidays.origin: Created by Pennsylvania-based author and speaker Dr. Rita Emmett, who wrote 'The Procrastinator's Handbook,' as a lighthearted push to stop delaying tasks.
holidays.funFact: The word procrastinate comes from the Latin 'pro' (forward) and 'cras' (tomorrow), literally meaning 'to put off until tomorrow.'

holidays.name: National Read a Book Day
holidays.description: A day to put down your phone, crack open a book, and get lost in a story. Any genre counts, from epic novels to cereal boxes if you're desperate.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that took hold in the early 2010s, promoted by book lovers and literacy advocates as a simple reminder to read for pleasure.
holidays.funFact: Studies have suggested that just six minutes of reading can reduce stress levels significantly, with some research claiming it works better than listening to music or taking a walk.

holidays.name: Bring Your Manners to Work Day
holidays.description: A day to say please, thank you, and maybe stop reply-all-ing to the entire company. Practice workplace courtesy and be a delight to your coworkers.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance promoted in workplace and etiquette circles, encouraging politeness and respect on the job.
holidays.funFact: The word 'etiquette' comes from an old French word meaning 'ticket' or 'label,' and was reportedly tied to the cards at the court of Louis XIV that listed rules of conduct.

holidays.name: Fight Procrastination Day's Cousin: Eat Beans Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek bean appreciation observance where legume lovers celebrate the humble, protein-packed, and famously musical fruit.
holidays.origin: Part of the loosely organized world of food calendar observances that celebrate everyday ingredients, shared by bean enthusiasts online.
holidays.funFact: Beans are among the oldest cultivated crops in the world, with evidence of farming going back thousands of years in the Americas and the Middle East.
